items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The helper is clearly named and has a docstring: `def punycode(domain): """Return the Punycode of the given domain if it's non-ASCII."""`. The call sites are short and match the reference style. Placing the helper after DEFAULT_LOCALE_ENCODING is a trivial nit.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It does add one reusable helper and converts at the source. But it converts twice: `make_msgid(domain=punycode(str(DNS_NAME)))` on top of `get_fqdn`. It also keeps the now-redundant `try: domain.encode('ascii') except UnicodeEncodeError:` wrapper in sanitize_address.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No errors are swallowed and no new try/except was added. The IDNA encode raises UnicodeError on invalid input instead of quietly producing a bad header. No magic constants.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: `self._fqdn = punycode(socket.getfqdn())` converts once at the source, for every encoding. Running punycode again in make_msgid does nothing to ASCII input, so nothing gets double-encoded. ASCII hostnames pass through unchanged. The hidden tests pass.
